approach: Add one module, crates/athena-core/src/reading/coverage.rs, with `check_reading_coverage(reading, request)`, wired as one `step!` line in `refusing_check` after `check_scope_limit`. It reads the request's `Acceptance:` section into bullets (a wrapped bullet's continuation lines join it), reduces each bullet and criterion to content stems, and never strips a prose-repeated word. A bullet's score is the plain share of its own stems found in its best criterion, so one reworded word lowers the score by one stem and never zeroes it. This revision replaces the min(A,B) / rare-stem share (finding 1). Instead, a criterion is excluded as evidence for bullet b when a sibling bullet s claims it, meaning it holds a word only s has, holds no word only b has, and matches s better than b. That targets the shared-framing failure directly and leaves a paraphrased criterion alone. Fixtures give ttnw and bp5e realistic framing-sharing siblings, and a pinned 'elapsed time' test records the outcome (finding 1). The replay test moves into refusal_corpus.rs, where `cases()` is in scope (finding 2). The paraphrase corpus cases replace the copied criteria with the recorded criterion text (finding 3). The plan and output say that criterion 2 holds verbatim only for the quoted bullet and criterion strings, and that the verification replay over recorded readings with the 15% hold is the real check on recorded shapes (finding 4). An omitted bullet refuses the reading, naming it, unless the non-bullet text affirmatively names a split of the job, request or work. Readings that ask a question or decline, and requests with no Acceptance heading, are not checked. The fake reader (fake.rs) and drain.rs change only if the suites fail without it.

decisions.choice: Score a bullet as the best plain share of its own stems over the criteria that no sibling bullet claims. Stems: lowercase alphanumeric runs, a fixed stop list, tokens under 2 characters dropped, then suffix stripping (ing, ed, es, s; only when 3 or more characters remain and the word does not end in ss), then a trailing e dropped and a doubled final consonant after ed/ing collapsed (not l, s, z). share(b,c) = |stems(b) ∩ stems(c)| / |stems(b)|, compared in u64 cross-multiplication as share*100 >= COVERAGE_MIN_PERCENT*|stems(b)|. COVERAGE_MIN_PERCENT starts at 35 (an estimate) and is set from the printed tuning table. Criterion c is claimed over bullet b by sibling s (another Acceptance bullet) when (stems(s) minus stems(b)) shares a stem with c, (stems(b) minus stems(s)) shares none with c, and share(s,c) > share(b,c). A claimed criterion is not evidence for b. A bullet with no stems after the stop list is covered. Out-of-scope items never count.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. Paraphrasing b's own rare word ('unchanged' written as 'identical') costs one stem of the plain share and is not zeroed. The claim rule applies only where a criterion has a word only a sibling has and none that only b has. Take the ttnw pair as an example: b1 'a test: with no improvement requests queued, ordering is unchanged' and a sibling b2 'with improvement requests queued, they are ordered first'. The recorded criterion for b1 holds 'test', which only b1 has, so b2 cannot claim it. b1 scores about 4 of 6 stems (about 67%, an estimate to be printed by the tuning test). For the sza7 shape, the criterion 'The status list shows each job's state' holds 'state' (only the sibling has it), lacks 'duration', and matches the sibling at 100% against about 80%, so it is claimed and cannot cover the duration bullet. A criterion that paraphrases 'duration' as 'elapsed time' and holds no sibling-only word is accepted, and the test pins that. No word is discarded and no bullet can become empty or vacuously covered, which was the rejection of 20261029-111121-fzx0. For a one-bullet request there are no siblings, so the score is the plain share.

rejected.option: min(A, B) with B the share of the bullet's lowest-df stems (the round-2 plan)
rejected.why: Finding 1: one reworded rare word zeroes B, so ttnw's 'unchanged' written as 'identical' would be refused against a framing-sharing sibling.

rejected.option: B over all stems below the bullet's highest df
rejected.why: It still scores 0 or low whenever the few distinguishing words are paraphrased, and it depends on how many siblings the request has.

rejected.option: Strip words the request prose repeats and require stem uniqueness
rejected.why: The rejected design of 20261029-111121-fzx0: a bullet whose distinguishing words the prose repeats becomes empty and is vacuously covered.

rejected.option: Plain share against the best single criterion with no claim rule (the round-1 plan)
rejected.why: A criterion written for a sibling shares the framing words and covers the dropped bullet (sza7).

rejected.option: One-to-one assignment of criteria to bullets
rejected.why: A legitimate criterion covering two bullets would leave one uncovered and wrongly refuse a reading that covers every bullet.

rejected.option: A model call to judge coverage
rejected.why: Reading checks are deterministic and call no model (checks.rs doc comments).

decisions.choice: Parse the Acceptance section line by line, untrimmed. The section starts after a line that is 'Acceptance:' or 'Acceptance criteria:' (trimmed, case-insensitive, leading # or * ignored). A line whose trimmed text passes `is_bullet` starts a bullet. A non-empty non-bullet line directly after a bullet or its continuation (no blank line between) is joined to that bullet when it is indented, or when the previous line does not end in '.', '!', '?' or ':' and the line is not a heading (a line ending in ':' or starting 'Files:' or 'Priority:'). Blank lines are skipped. The section ends at a heading line, or at a non-bullet line after a blank line. Requests with no Acceptance heading are not checked. The marker and a leading '[tag]' are removed before stemming.
decisions.reason: A hard-wrapped bullet is scored on its whole text and the bullets after it are still checked. Bare bullet lists without a heading are in many existing requests and tests (corpus cases star-bullets, numbered-dot-parts, job_plan.rs:166); checking them would refuse lists the owner never marked as acceptance. `is_bullet` (topics.rs:266) is reused read-only, so `request_text_acceptance` (topics.rs:276, used by `athena plan`) does not change.

rejected.option: End the section at the first non-bullet line
rejected.why: A wrapped bullet's continuation ends the section and later bullets go unchecked.

rejected.option: Treat every bullet in the request as acceptance, as request_text_acceptance does
rejected.why: It widens the refusal rate far past the estimate and refuses plain lists.

decisions.choice: A request allows a split only when a sentence of its non-bullet text (split by `sentences`, checks.rs:332, lowercased, curly apostrophes straightened) has a whole-phrase match (`has_phrase`, surveys.rs:39) on a modal ('may', 'can', 'could', 'free to', 'allowed to', 'ok to', 'okay to') followed by 'split' and a job object ('this job', 'the job', 'this request', 'the request', 'this work', 'the work', 'it into jobs', 'it into parts', 'it into follow-ups', 'it into separate jobs', 'into separate jobs', 'into follow-up jobs', 'into follow-ups'), or on the imperatives 'split this job', 'split the job', 'split this request', 'split the request'. The sentence must hold no negation token (not, never, no, cannot, without, avoid, forbid, forbidden, 'instead of', any word ending in n't, 'dont') and no '?'.
decisions.reason: 'Do not split this job' has a negation and allows nothing. Ordinary code prose ('Split the log line into fields', 'split it on commas', 'Split the output into two columns') names no job, request or work, so it matches no phrase and the check stays on. 'Should we split this job?' is a question and allows nothing. A refused reading can still ask the split as a question.

rejected.option: Any occurrence of the word 'split' allows a split
rejected.why: 'Do not split this job' would disable the check, the sza7 failure.

rejected.option: Bare 'split into' or 'split it' as permission
rejected.why: They match code prose and turn the check off for the whole request.

decisions.choice: Move the fixture replay into crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs as `coverage_replay_over_the_corpus_and_recorded_shapes`, modeled on `delivery_verb_replay_over_the_cited_jobs`. The corpus replay runs `check_reading_coverage` over every `cases()` entry with a reading and asserts that every refusal is a case whose expected outcome is Refuse("check_reading_coverage"). It also asserts that no case that is not expected to refuse here is refused by it. It prints 'coverage replay: N readings, R refused by check_reading_coverage, 0 readings that cover every bullet refused; of the M corpus readings accepted before this check, 0 are newly refused'.

risks.risk: The claim rule still refuses a reading that covers a bullet only through a merged paraphrase, for example one criterion 'status list shows job state and elapsed time' covering both the state and the duration bullets. The state sibling claims it, so the duration bullet is refused. That raises the refusal rate above the 10% estimate.
risks.mitigation: The refusal names the bullet and its score, and the one correction is to word the criterion with the bullet's own words. The pinned test records this outcome as a known limit. The tuning table prints scores. The verification replay measures the real rate against the 15% hold.

risks.risk: A framing-only criterion such as 'The status list shows jobs' covers every sibling that shares the framing, so a dropped bullet can slip through when such a criterion exists.
risks.mitigation: This is the price of accepting paraphrase (finding 1). The check is a floor, not a proof of coverage, and the pinned test records the outcome. The sza7 shape, where the reading wrote a criterion per remaining bullet in their own words, is still refused.

risks.risk: The recorded sza7, ttnw and bp5e texts are not in the snapshot, because records/ is absent. Only the quoted bullet and criterion strings are verbatim and the siblings are rebuilt, so the tuned threshold rests on a small sample (finding 4).
risks.mitigation: Each fixture is labelled 'rebuilt, records absent'. The siblings are chosen to share framing, which is the harder case. If a recorded text is available the producer replaces the rebuilt fixture and re-tunes from the printed table. The verification replay over recorded readings, held above 15%, is the real check on recorded shapes.

risks.risk: A closing sentence directly under the last bullet with no blank line is joined to that bullet and lowers its share.
risks.mitigation: Joining stops at a blank line, a heading, or a previous line that ends a sentence. The wrapped-bullet test pins both the join and the stop, and the refusal text shows the bullet text it scored.

risks.risk: The phrase list misses an affirmative split wording and refuses a request whose owner allowed a split.
risks.mitigation: A refused reading can ask the split as a question, which is not checked. The phrase table pins accepted and refused forms, including code-prose lookalikes.

risks.risk: The corpus INPUT_FORMS array has a fixed size, so a forgotten length bump or an unused tag fails `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms`.
risks.mitigation: Step 8 sets the length to 62 for ten new tags and each tag is carried by a case named in the plan. The demonstration for criterion 5 runs the corpus test.

risks.risk: The fake reader and hestia, steward or cli tests fail after the check is wired.
risks.mitigation: Step 10 runs the athena-core, athena-agent and athena-cli suites and applies per-bullet fake criteria; criterion 10 limits the diff to fake.rs and drain.rs.

risks.risk: The corpus replay figure is trivially 0 newly refused for pre-existing cases, because `base_reading` copies every bullet. It could be mistaken for the history rate.
risks.mitigation: The printed line and the CHANGELOG label it a chosen sample. The declared 10% stays an estimate, checked at verification by the replay over recorded readings against the 15% hold.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `coverage_names_the_omitted_bullet_and_accepts_full_cover` in crates/athena-core/src/reading/coverage.rs. The sza7 request is rebuilt with three Acceptance bullets that share the framing 'The status list shows each job's ...' (state, owner, duration), labelled 'rebuilt, records absent'. A reading with criteria for the state and owner bullets only goes through `check_reading_coverage`, and a reading with a criterion per bullet goes through it too. A second test, `coverage_sibling_bullet_is_not_covered_by_shared_framing`, runs the reading whose only criterion is 'The status list shows each job's state'.
demonstrations.observes: The omitting reading returns Err whose text contains the duration bullet, and the phrase 'acceptance bullet'. The state-only reading also returns Err naming the duration bullet (the criterion is claimed by the state sibling), which a plain-share scorer with no claim rule would have accepted. The full-cover reading returns Ok. Corpus case coverage-omitted-bullet-sza7-refused shows `refusing_check` naming `check_reading_coverage`. The last line is 'test result: ok'.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, or if the bullet is not named, the Err assertion fails. Without the claim rule the sibling-framing assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `check_reading_coverage` (added by step 2), reached through `refusing_check` (exists, checks.rs:518). The fixture is a local `fn reading(criteria: &[&str]) -> Reading` in the coverage.rs tests module (added by step 5), built as the corpus `base_reading` does (refusal_corpus.rs:161), taking criteria as plain strings. `use super::*` reaches `Reading`. The scoring is not duplicated in the test.

demonstrations.method: Test `coverage_accepts_the_recorded_ttnw_and_bp5e_paraphrases` in coverage.rs and corpus cases coverage-paraphrased-ttnw-accepted and coverage-paraphrased-bp5e-accepted. Each request has a framing-sharing sibling. For ttnw, bullet 1 is 'a test: with no improvement requests queued, ordering is unchanged' and sibling 2 is 'with improvement requests queued, they are ordered first'. Their criteria are the recorded text 'a new test with no Steward or Hestia requests queued asserts the plan order is identical…' for bullet 1 and a copy of bullet 2. For bp5e, bullet 1 is 'The root cause is named in the change description and fixed where it originates' (its text is the one in `root_cause_request`, refusal_corpus.rs:282) and the sibling is 'A test fails without the change and passes with it'. The criterion for bullet 1 is the recorded 'its doc comment names the root cause'. The corpus cases replace `case.reading.acceptance_criteria` with those criteria so they do not copy the bullets (finding 3). Only the bullet and criterion strings quoted in the brief are verbatim; the rest of each request is rebuilt, because records/ is absent from every snapshot (finding 4). The real check on the recorded shapes is the verification replay over recorded readings with the 15% hold. `coverage_threshold_is_tuned_on_the_recorded_shapes` prints each bullet's best score and asserts min covered score >= COVERAGE_MIN_PERCENT > max omitted score. Its fixtures are ttnw, bp5e, sza7 and sibling-framing, and the pinned 'elapsed time' shapes of criterion 3's neighbour test `coverage_paraphrased_rare_word_is_pinned`. That test pins three outcomes: a criterion 'Each row of the status list shows the elapsed time of the job' is accepted for the duration bullet; 'The status list shows jobs' is accepted (a known limit: a framing-only criterion covers all siblings); and 'status list shows job state and elapsed time' is refused (a merged paraphrase is claimed by the state sibling, a known limit).
demonstrations.observes: Zero refusals on the ttnw and bp5e shapes. The printed table shows each recorded bullet at or above the threshold (producer reads the actual numbers: ttnw is about 4 of 6 stems and bp5e about 3 of 7, both estimates from hand-stemming, and the table replaces them). The paraphrase pin shows its three chosen outcomes. The tuning test passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: A scorer that does not stem queued/queue, ordering/order and names/named, a threshold above the covered scores, or a rare-stem share that zeroes a reworded word, refuses these shapes and the zero-refusal assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: `check_reading_coverage` and the pure scorer `coverage_gaps(request, criteria)`, both added by step 2. The fixtures are consts in the coverage.rs tests module (step 5), passed as plain strings. The corpus cases use the existing `case()` helper (refusal_corpus.rs:230), with `case.reading.acceptance_criteria` assigned (added by step 7); `Case.reading` is a pub field.

demonstrations.method: Test `coverage_judges_words_the_prose_repeats`. The request prose says 'The duration column shows seconds', and one Acceptance bullet is 'The duration column shows seconds'; another bullet about a different topic is covered. Reading A has criteria only for the other bullet. Reading B adds a criterion containing 'duration', 'column' and 'seconds'. Both go through `check_reading_coverage`. Corpus cases coverage-prose-repeated-words-refused and coverage-prose-repeated-words-covered-accepted run the same shapes through `refusing_check`.
demonstrations.observes: A returns Err naming the bullet. B returns Ok. The bullet's words are scored even though the prose repeats them.
demonstrations.fails_without: The rejected design that strips prose-repeated words leaves the bullet empty, so A is accepted and the Err assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: `check_reading_coverage` (step 2) with the local `reading()` fixture (step 5); the request is a const string in the test. The corpus cases use `case()` (exists) with a criterion removed (added by step 7).

demonstrations.method: Test `coverage_a_split_is_allowed_only_when_affirmed`. The same request, with a dropped bullet, runs with 'You may split this job.', 'Do not split this job.', 'Split the output into two columns.' and with no split line. `request_allows_split` also runs over a phrase table. Allowed: 'You may split this job.'; 'Feel free to split this job into follow-ups.'; 'It is ok to split the request into separate jobs.'. Not allowed: 'Do not split this job', 'never split it into jobs', "don't split the job", "can't split this job", 'without splitting', 'Should we split this job?', 'Split the log line into fields.', 'split it on commas', 'Split the output into two columns.'. Corpus cases coverage-split-allowed-accepted, coverage-split-negated-refused and coverage-split-lookalike-prose-refused run these through `refusing_check`.
demonstrations.observes: Only the affirmative request returns Ok. The negated, silent and code-prose requests return Err naming the dropped bullet. The table gives the expected booleans.
demonstrations.fails_without: A rule that treats any 'split', 'split into' or 'split it' as permission accepts 'Do not split this job' or the code-prose rows, so an Err assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: `check_reading_coverage` and `request_allows_split`, both added by step 2, with the local `reading()` fixture and const requests (step 5). The corpus cases are added by step 7.

demonstrations.observes: All corpus tests pass, including `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome`, `the_wrapper_agrees_with_refusing_check_on_every_case` and the replay. The refusing cases are coverage-omitted-bullet-sza7-refused, coverage-sibling-framing-refused, coverage-star-bullet-omitted-refused, coverage-number-dot-omitted-refused, coverage-wrapped-bullet-omitted-refused, coverage-prose-repeated-words-refused, coverage-split-negated-refused and coverage-split-lookalike-prose-refused. The Grep returns exactly one match in checks.rs.

demonstrations.method: Test `coverage_replay_over_the_corpus_and_recorded_shapes` in crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs (step 7). It runs `check_reading_coverage` over every `cases()` entry (in scope there) and asserts every refusal is a case expecting Refuse("check_reading_coverage") and no other case is refused by it. It prints the replay line described in Decision 6. Test `reading_coverage_refusal_is_declared_intended` reads the declared share with `athena_core::reading::replay_declaration` from the criterion text 'expected 10% of newly refused readings' and expects Some(10), so the hold limit is 15. The criterion text and the CHANGELOG say that 10 is an estimate, that the printed figure covers a chosen sample, and that the verification replay measures the real rate over recorded readings and holds the job above 15%.
demonstrations.observes: The printed replay line, a declared share of 10 and the 15% hold limit. No reading that covers every bullet is refused.
demonstrations.fails_without: A scorer that refuses a covered paraphrase fails the no-covered-reading-refused assertion. A criterion without the exact 'N% of newly refused readings' form makes `replay_declaration` return no share.
demonstrations.seam: `check_reading_coverage` (step 2) and `replay_declaration` (exists, replay.rs:263), called from the integration test crate. `cases()` is the test's input, not a double. The replay test is added by step 7. No history replay exists in the snapshot, so the figure is over the corpus.

demonstrations.method: The new test `reading_coverage_refusal_is_declared_intended`, modeled on `history_fixture_refusal_is_declared_intended` (refusal_corpus.rs:2916), collapses white space in `include_str!("../../../CHANGELOG.md")` and asserts the substrings 'check_reading_coverage', 'refuses more readings', 'higher refusal rate is intended', 'expected 10% of newly refused readings', 'estimate' and 'verification replay'.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes. `## [Unreleased]` in CHANGELOG.md holds the entry under Added.
demonstrations.fails_without: A missing entry or a changed phrase fails an assertion.
demonstrations.seam: `include_str!` of CHANGELOG.md, a pattern already used in this file (refusal_corpus.rs:2953). The test is added by step 7.

demonstrations.method: The same test reads the contiguous `///` lines above `pub fn check_reading_coverage(` from `reading_source()` (coverage.rs added to it by step 7, before reading.rs) and asserts the needles '20261029-084645-sza7', '[`check_reading_acceptance`]', 'a split may be proposed only as a question, never by dropping a bullet', 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' and 'estimate'. No attribute line sits between the doc and the fn, because the scan stops at the first non-`///` line.

demonstrations.method: After `cargo test --locked` passes, run git status and git diff --stat and read the changed paths.
demonstrations.observes: The changed paths are a subset of the seven deliverables. fake.rs appears only if the athena-core, athena-agent or athena-cli suite failed without it, and then its diff is only the added per-bullet criteria and a test for them. drain.rs appears only if a cli test still failed after the fake.rs change.

open_questions: Host: records/ is absent from the planner and producer snapshots, so the verbatim request and reading texts of jobs sza7, ttnw and bp5e cannot be read. The plan assumes the producer's sandbox lacks them too and relies on the quoted bullet and criterion strings. If the sandbox holds the recorded texts, the producer replaces the rebuilt fixtures and re-tunes.
